card.summary: Open-source software that the user installs and runs: the full Temporal platform on the user's own infrastructure at no cost from Temporal, started locally w...

free_tier.stated: Open-source software that the user installs and runs: the full Temporal platform on the user's own infrastructure at no cost from Temporal, started locally with temporal server start-dev; the open-source quickstart needs no credit card
free_tier.notes: Temporal Cloud (dev-services/temporal-cloud) is the hosted offer and comes first.

per_object_cap.stated: Payloads (the Workflow context and each Workflow and Activity argument and return value): Temporal warns at 512 KB and errors at 2 MB; a gRPC message is limited to 4 MB
per_object_cap.notes: defaults coded into the server; a Workflow History is also capped at 50 MB or 51,200 Events

retention.stated: closed Workflow Execution histories are kept for the Namespace's Retention Period, which is at least 1 day and defaults to 3 days when a Namespace is created with the temporal CLI and no value
retention.notes: On the development server (temporal server start-dev), Workflow Executions are lost when the server process dies unless --db-filename sets a persistent store.

egress.terms: not set by the software: Workers and clients connect to the user's own Temporal Service, so the network terms of the host that runs it apply

record.interface_detail: the Frontend Service exposes a gRPC Proto API on port 7233 that the Temporal SDKs use (the vocabulary has no gRPC term); an HTTP API is switched on in the server's static configuration (httpPort, 7243 in the Nexus example) and on the development server with --http-port; the temporal CLI interacts with the running server, and the development server serves the Web UI at port 8233
record.tooling: the user installs and runs the Temporal server on a rented or free machine: temporal server start-dev from the temporal CLI (a single binary with no external dependencies), the Docker Compose example (PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch), the Temporal Server and UI Server Go binaries, or the Helm charts on Kubernetes; the Temporal SDKs (Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, .NET, Ruby, PHP) and the temporal CLI.
record.chaining: Last resort after the hosted durable-execution offers (the hosted Inngest free tier in dev-services/inngest, and Temporal Cloud in dev-services/temporal-cloud): the user's own Workers connect to a Temporal Service that the user installs and keeps running.

limits.value: Payloads: warning at 512 KB and error at 2 MB; a gRPC message is limited to 4 MB
Workflow History: error at 50 MB or 51,200 Events, which terminates the Workflow Execution

record.limits_note: The open source Temporal Service has a default limit of 2,000 pending Activities, Child Workflows, Signals or Workflow cancellation requests, which the dynamic configuration overrides.
record.binding_note: The documentation states no quota for the open-source server; the Persistence and Visibility stores and the machines that the user runs bound throughput, and the per-Workflow-Execution limits are defaults in the server.

identity_cost.detail: No account with Temporal is needed: the open-source quickstart installs the temporal CLI (brew install temporal) and runs temporal server start-dev on the local machine, and a credit card is required only to sign up for Temporal Cloud.

record.reliability_note: The development server is not intended for production use, skips certain HTTP security checks, and loses Workflow Executions when its process dies unless --db-filename sets a persistent store. A production Temporal Service needs data stores for persistence that the user creates and maintains, has no role-based access control or audit logging out of the box, and its hosts should not be accessible from the public internet; Temporal does not guarantee support for the server.
record.confidence_note: Install paths, defaults, limits, retention and interfaces are read on first-party documentation pages; the server was not installed or run, and no execution quota for the open-source server is stated on those pages.
